channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Russia Sign Agreement on Judicial Cooperation and AI
item.description: Kazakhstan and Russia aim to expand cooperation, including in the legal sphere. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated this during a meeting with the Chairman of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, Igor Krasnov. The countries plan to exchange experience, develop digital technologies, and utilize artificial intelligence in their courts. Joint training for judicial staff is also anticipated.

item.title: New Environmental Requirements for Almaty Cafes and Baths to Reduce Emissions
item.description: Almaty is continuing efforts to reduce harmful emissions from small and medium-sized businesses. Specialists are explaining new environmental requirements to owners of cafes, bathhouses, and service stations. The new rules will limit the use of coal and liquid fuels in gasified areas of low-emission zones. These regulations aim to improve air quality for residents.

item.title: SCO and ECO Foreign Ministers Discuss Economic Cooperation in Islamabad
item.description: Delegations from the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) met in Islamabad for the 30th session of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers. Discussions focused on strengthening ECO's potential as a platform for multilateral interaction in political and economic spheres. Participants signed the Islamabad Communiqué and approved Strategic Economic Cooperation Goals until 2035.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explains Why Kempir-Abad Reservoir Won't Be Filled to Full Capacity
item.description: Uzbekistan will not fill the Kempir-Abad (Andijan) reservoir to its original design volume of over 1.9 billion cubic meters. According to agreements with Kyrgyzstan, the maximum volume is set at 1.574 billion cubic meters. Uzbekistan's Minister of Water Resources, Shavkat Khamraev, stated that the agreed-upon volume is sufficient for the country's needs, as higher levels could increase flooding in adjacent areas.

item.title: Kazakhstan Minister Denies State Control Over Social Media
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Culture and Information, Arman Kyryqbayev, stated that his ministry lacks the authority to arbitrarily restrict social media accounts or interfere with their operations. He denied the existence of state mechanisms for intimidating citizens online.

item.title: Two Teenagers Injured by Airgun in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy Region Undergo Surgery
item.description: Two teenagers in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region, injured by an airgun, are in stable condition and will undergo surgery to remove the pellets. They were hospitalized at the National Center for Mother and Child Protection. A 24-year-old suspect has been detained.

item.title: Kazakh President Receives Chairman of the Supreme Court of Russia
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Igor Krasnov, Chairman of Russia's Supreme Court. They discussed the unique nature of Kazakhstan-Russia relations, built on shared history and mutual respect. Tokayev highlighted ongoing political reforms in Kazakhstan. Krasnov noted active cooperation between the courts, including a first-ever agreement on cooperation between the high judicial instances of both countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Belarus to Abolish Mandatory Registration for Stays Under 30 Days
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Belarus will abolish mandatory registration for citizens staying in the other country for up to 30 days. The agreement, signed in September 2025, aims to simplify travel and boost economic and tourism ties. This change will apply to citizens of Kyrgyzstan temporarily in Belarus and Belarusian citizens in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: New Russian Crypto Rules May Shift Operations Away from Kyrgyzstan, Expert Warns
item.description: New cryptocurrency regulations in Russia, effective July 1, 2027, could lead to a migration of foreign economic activity operations from Kyrgyzstan to Russian infrastructure. An expert noted that Russia's developing regulated environment might attract companies currently using Kyrgyzstan for such transactions, though Kyrgyzstan may retain some advantages.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Russia Sign Cooperation Agreement Between Supreme Courts
item.description: The Supreme Courts of Kazakhstan and Russia have signed a cooperation agreement, marking a first in their judicial history. The agreement aims to foster professional dialogue, advance judicial digitalization, and explore the implementation of artificial intelligence in justice systems. This follows a meeting between Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Russian Supreme Court Chairman Igor Krasnov.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Introduce Visa-Free Regime for Citizens of 18 More Countries
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to implement a visa-free regime for citizens of 18 additional countries and extend the visa-free stay duration from 30 to 60 days. This initiative aims to address issues faced by tourists planning long-term expeditions in the country, facilitating easier travel and longer stays for international visitors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Travel Company Head Arrested for Umrah Pilgrimage Fraud
item.description: The head of "Nur Umra Travel" was arrested for alleged fraud in organizing Umrah pilgrimages. Over 100 Kyrgyz citizens were reportedly unable to travel from Tashkent, Uzbekistan, after purchasing travel packages. The company allegedly failed to register pilgrims and demanded extra fees. A criminal case for fraud has been initiated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Pregnant women face difficulties accessing free essential medications
item.description: Pregnant women in Kyrgyzstan are struggling to obtain free iron, folic acid, and iodine supplements, despite state provision. The issue is particularly acute in rural areas, with women unable to access medications even with a 90% discount. The Health Minister stated that three types of anemia prevention drugs are free under the state guarantee program.

item.title: Youth Council to be Established Under Kazakhstan's Kurultai
item.description: A Youth Council will be formed under the first convocation of Kazakhstan's Kurultai. This new body aims to unite youth initiatives, promote them systematically, and establish direct dialogue between the younger generation and the Kurultai. It will include Kurultai deputies, representatives of youth organizations, and young professionals from various fields.

item.title: Illegal Motorcade in Kyzylorda Results in Fines and Court Cases
item.description: Police in Kyzylorda identified eight drivers who organized an illegal motorcade and violated traffic rules. Videos of dangerous maneuvers circulated on social media, leading to the identification and prosecution of the offenders. The drivers, aged 20-25, were charged with dangerous maneuvering and creating hazardous situations. Three faced court for petty hooliganism and were fined.

item.title: Europe Sees Sharp Rise in Superbug Infections, Raising Mortality Concerns
item.description: European hospitals are experiencing a significant increase in severe bloodstream infections caused by a drug-resistant 'superbug'. Over six years, cases have risen by 72%. The bacteria, Klebsiella pneumoniae, can cause pneumonia, meningitis, and sepsis. Some strains are resistant to nearly all antibiotics, increasing mortality risks. Strict disinfection and hygiene protocols are crucial.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Aktobe Businessman Murder Case
item.description: Police in Aktobe have arrested a suspect in the murder of a businessman. The Interior Ministry has dispatched experienced investigators to the region. The victim, a gas station owner, was shot dead at his home, and his car and valuables were stolen. The suspect is a citizen of Kazakhstan and a resident of Aktobe. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Investment and Job Creation Figures Presented by Cabinet Head
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's fixed capital investment reached 422.9 billion soms in January-October 2026, a 62.9% increase year-on-year. Foreign direct investment in 2025 was $1,310.8 million, growing 26% in the first half of 2026. The country created 273,000 jobs in 2025 and 88,300 in the first six months of 2026. International agencies affirmed Kyrgyzstan's credit ratings.

item.title: Nearly 1,000 International Observers Expected for Kyrgyzstan's Presidential Election
item.description: Approximately 1,000 international observers are anticipated to attend Kyrgyzstan's upcoming presidential election. The Central Election Commission has sent out invitations, with many countries confirming their participation. This number is similar to the 800 observers present in the previous election, with potential to reach 1,000 due to sustained international interest.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputy Proposes Audio Recording in Kindergartens Where Video is Prohibited
item.description: A deputy in Kazakhstan's Parliament has proposed continuous audio recording in kindergarten rooms where video surveillance is not permitted. This measure aims to enhance child safety, especially for children with special educational needs who may struggle to report abuse. Current standards, established in 2019, primarily focus on facility security and do not mandate audio recording.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Russia Sign First Cooperation Agreement Between Supreme Courts
item.description: Kazakhstan and Russia have signed their first cooperation agreement between their supreme courts. The agreement, established during a meeting between Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Russia's Supreme Court Chairman Igor Krasnov, aims to foster professional dialogue, judicial digitalization, and AI implementation. This strengthens the strategic partnership between the two nations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Muslims Urged to Avoid Umrah Travel Via Neighboring Countries
item.description: The Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Kyrgyzstan has advised citizens to temporarily avoid traveling for Umrah through neighboring countries. This follows an incident where 104 Kyrgyz pilgrims were stranded in Tashkent, unable to fly to Saudi Arabia. The situation prompted an emergency meeting involving Kyrgyz officials and the embassy in Uzbekistan to ensure the pilgrims' safety and arrange their return.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Construction Sector Grew by 61.5% in First 10 Months of the Year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's construction sector experienced a significant growth of 61.5% in the first 10 months of the current year, according to Cabinet Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. During this period, 291 social facilities worth 23.8 billion soms were built or renovated, including schools, kindergartens, healthcare, and cultural/sports facilities. Major projects like the "Rys Ordo" congress center and "Bishkek Arena" stadium were completed.

item.title: Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank (Kazakhstan) Joins Deposit Guarantee System
item.description: Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank (Kazakhstan), a subsidiary of a major UAE bank, has joined Kazakhstan's mandatory deposit guarantee system as of November 13, 2026. This means deposits, accounts, and card balances of individuals in the bank are now protected by the Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund (KDIF). The bank is the 21st participant, with guarantees covering tenge and foreign currency deposits up to specified limits.

item.title: 10 Hectares of Land Worth 113 Million Som Returned to State in Issyk-Kul
item.description: Ten hectares of agricultural land, valued at nearly 113 million soms, have been returned to state ownership in the Jeti-Oguz district of Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region. An investigation by the prosecutor's office revealed that in 2005, officials illegally transferred these lands to private ownership, violating land legislation. The prosecutor's office took measures to reclaim the land.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Investors in Financial Pyramids May Become Suspects
item.description: Kazakhstan investors in financial pyramids could face suspicion if authorities find evidence of them managing, participating in, or advertising the pyramid. The Economic Investigation Department in Almaty stated that each case is assessed individually. Investigators examine the number of new participants attracted and any signs of criminal activity by the investor.

item.title: China's President Calls for Deeper Cooperation in Science, Digital Economy, and AI
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged deeper cooperation in scientific innovation, the digital economy, and artificial intelligence during the APEC Leaders Week in Shenzhen. He emphasized supporting the post-WWII international order and resolving disputes through dialogue. Xi also called for removing trade barriers to foster an open Asia-Pacific economy and invited global businesses to collaborate with China.

item.title: Save the Children: 55% of Displaced Afghan Children Face Food Shortages
item.description: Save the Children reports that 55% of displaced children in Afghanistan face food shortages, with 41% experiencing deteriorating health. The report, based on interviews with over 800 children and caregivers, indicates that over 90% have experienced displacement. Access to education has declined for one-third, and economic poverty is identified as the main driver of displacement.

item.title: UK Launches Second Phase of Joint Program to Combat Malnutrition in Afghanistan
item.description: The UK Special Representative for Afghanistan, Richard Lindsay, announced the second phase of a joint program to combat malnutrition, implemented with UNICEF, WFP, and FAO. The program aims to improve nutritional support and early intervention. During the first phase, 520,000 caregivers received counseling, 40,000 children received supplements, and over 55,000 people received cash assistance.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Electricity Consumption Increased by 25% in the Last Five Years
item.description: Electricity consumption in Kyrgyzstan has grown by 25% over the past five years, according to the first deputy minister of energy. The increase is attributed to the commissioning of new facilities and a sharp rise in demand. Extensive work is underway to reconstruct aging hydroelectric power stations and build new transmission lines and modern facilities.

item.title: World Bank: Afghanistan's Economy Grows in Size but Shrinks Per Capita
item.description: The World Bank reports that Afghanistan's economy is growing in overall size but shrinking on a per capita basis due to population growth outpacing economic expansion. Projections indicate a 3% economic growth in FY2026, but with population growth exceeding 6%, per capita output is expected to decline for the third consecutive year. Agricultural recovery is a key driver of economic growth.

item.title: Over 11,000 Cases of ARVI and Flu Registered in Kyrgyzstan in One Week
item.description: Kyrgyzstan registered 11,439 cases of acute respiratory viral infections (ARVI) and flu between November 9 and 15, a 5% increase from the previous week. Children under 14 accounted for 67.9% of cases. Higher than average incidence rates were observed in Bishkek, Osh, and the Naryn, Issyk-Kul, and Chuy regions. Rhinovirus is the predominant circulating virus.

item.title: Kazakh businesses report declining demand and production in Q3 2026
item.description: A significant portion of Kazakh enterprises surveyed by the National Bank reported a decrease in demand, production output, and capacity utilization in the third quarter of 2026. The diffusion index for demand fell to 48.7, with industry at 49.4 and services at 48. Production output also saw a decline, with the index at 49.4.

item.title: Central Asia Warehouse Market Summit in Almaty anticipates market equilibrium
item.description: The CAWS 2026 Summit in Almaty, attended by over 350 professionals from 13 countries, discussed the Central Asian warehouse market. A new index, 'Central Asia Warehouse Market Pulse,' scored 48.1 out of 100, indicating a slight contraction. 52% expect demand and supply to balance within a year, while 81% of developers plan new projects.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan tour company head arrested over alleged scam leaving 100+ pilgrims stranded
item.description: The head of the 'Nur Umra Travel' company has been detained in Bishkek on suspicion of fraud. Over 100 Kyrgyz citizens were left stranded in Tashkent, unable to fly to Saudi Arabia for Umrah due to a lack of visas and tickets. The company allegedly failed to register pilgrims and demanded extra fees.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Proposes Gas Tariff Subsidies for Winter Heating
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has proposed subsidizing natural gas tariffs for residents during winter months. The MP highlighted the significant initial costs of installing gas heating systems, which can be a financial burden for households. While the government already subsidizes fuel, the proposal for gas tariff subsidies requires further calculation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Procedures for Troubled Bank Sanitation
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Justice has registered new regulations governing the sanitation of troubled banks, aiming to protect depositors' rights and ensure banking service continuity. The new rules outline three main tools: asset and liability transfer to another bank, creation of an intermediate bank, or capital write-down/conversion. Depositor funds are protected, with guaranteed deposits not being written down or converted.

item.title: Kazakhstan MP Highlights Challenges in Educating Hearing-Impaired Children
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kazakhstan has pointed out significant problems in the education system for children with hearing impairments. The MP urged the government to establish a continuous rehabilitation system post-cochlear implantation, noting that while surgeries are funded, long-term rehabilitation is lacking, especially in regional areas. Communication difficulties between parents and children were also highlighted.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Launches System for Direct Salary Payments to Any Bank Card
item.description: Uzbek citizens can now receive salaries and bonuses directly to any bank card or e-wallet, regardless of their employer's bank. The Central Bank has introduced the "Funds Distribution Center" system to facilitate this. Previously, employees had to use cards from their employer's designated bank. This new system initially targets private sector organizations and their employees, with plans for future expansion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Signs Over 90 Investment Agreements Worth $11.8 Billion in Three Years
item.description: Over 90 investment agreements totaling $11.8 billion have been signed in Kyrgyzstan over the past three years, according to Ravshanbek Sabirov, head of the National Investment Agency. He stated this at the Asia Innovation Forum 2026 in Bishkek. Sabirov highlighted the country's interest in attracting international venture funds and technology companies to foster sustainable development and innovation.
